craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of sealing — utsāha as measure, course, denial, seal land in turn. Measure without unit: One-short kept obscure per BOUNDARY (ekahānyā held open — no smoothing); examples do the measuring (kings man, brahmins). Rejected: (a) defining the unit → killed by BOUNDARY: prose never defines it. (b) cutting examples → killed: examples ARE the measure. Read aloud: ONE-short — YET-by THE-chief, BY the PURE — … THE-king's-MAN, AND the BRAH-min's.

lines: One short — yet by the chief, by the pure — secondaries fit each other —
the king's man, and the brahmin's.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ekahānyā pradhānena śuddhenānyānyayogitā syādguṇasya yathā rājñaḥ puruṣo brāhmaṇasya ca
notes: ekahānyā held open (one short of what?)

reads_against.argmap: How do secondaries fit the chief? → Secondaries fit the chief one-short of pure: king's man, brahmin's.
c1_essence: Secondaries measured against chiefs — king's man, brahmin's; other chiefs, other unities — king's horse, man (vv19-20).
Course told, delusion denied, seal spoken: Māyā-knower-resting intellects drive transaction, moment-grounded in self-awareness; told, proved, unrefuted, useful, full apparatus besides (vv21-23).
